name: Tobiah
title: Ammonite Opponent of Jerusalem's Rebuilding
summary: Tobiah was an Ammonite official who, together with Sanballat, actively opposed Nehemiah and the Jews in their work to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. He used threats, mockery, and political intrigue in an attempt to halt the reconstruction efforts but failed. He also had family connections among the Jewish nobility, which gave him influence in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Tobiah Mocks the Rebuilding Effort
keyEvents.description: Tobiah ridiculed the Jews' attempt to rebuild the wall, saying that even a fox could knock down the stone wall they were building.

keyEvents.title: Conspiracy Against Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Tobiah, Sanballat, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod plotted together to attack Jerusalem and create confusion in order to stop the construction of the wall.

keyEvents.title: Attempt to Lure Nehemiah into a Trap
keyEvents.description: Tobiah and Sanballat sent repeated messages to Nehemiah, trying to lure him to a meeting on the plain of Ono in order to harm him, but Nehemiah rejected the invitations.

keyEvents.title: Threatening letters to Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Tobiah sent letters to Nehemiah to frighten him and tried to weaken his resolve through threats and false accusations of rebellion against the Persian king.

keyEvents.title: Tobiah's influence among Jewish nobility
keyEvents.description: Many of the leading men in Judah had family ties with Tobiah through marriage, and they spoke well of him to Nehemiah and reported Nehemiah's words back to Tobiah.

keyEvents.title: Tobiah expelled from the temple chamber
keyEvents.description: When Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem after an absence, he discovered that the priest Eliashib had given Tobiah a large room in the temple. Nehemiah threw out all of Tobiah's belongings and cleansed the rooms.
